findings: 3+1 exclusivity cluster (INERT per calibration, not scored): A, C and D each name a depth stratum of the bed, B speaks of the bed as a whole.

findings: FORM PROFILE (the point of this pass). Consequence connective: “so” in A and D, 2/4, balanced. Explicit negation: A (“has not had”) and B (“no wax”), 2/4, balanced. Hedges and modals: 0/4, balanced, and critically there is no lone hedged option. Opening word class: pronoun in A and D, gerund in B, determiner-NP in C - two singletons, so the variable points at no single option. Word counts 17/16/17/15, no isolate. Coordinate vs subordinate: A and D are two-clause coordinate, B is a pseudo-cleft with a finite free relative, C is one clause with coordinated VPs.

THE FORM DEFECT THE PREVIOUS ROUND INTRODUCED IS CLOSED. The three highest-signal form variables - consequence connective, explicit negation, hedge - are each balanced 2+2 or 0+4, and no option is the unique value of any of them.

Residual weak isolates exist but name three different options and none converges: B alone carries a finite embedded clause and the strict universal “all day”; C alone has a grammatical subject that is not the schools (“A membrane under them”) and the longest internal run; A alone carries a hard number (“nine years”).

FORM AND CONTENT DIVERGE, which is the safe configuration: the weak form isolate is B while the content-favoured option is C, so no compound route exists. Contrast las-b22-003 q2, where they converge.

Residual content channel, PAIR_STRUCTURE 2+2: A and D both explain the observation away as an artefact of his comparison (“nine years of hooves”; “the change falls between his two grids”), while B and C both assert the bed does not change through the day. PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE then collapses the set - the stem asks what is suggested about the schools, not about his measurement schedule, so A and D read as off-stem and the residual is B and C at 0.50.

The tie-break from B to C is WORLD_KNOWLEDGE and expert-only: it is waxed footing, not unwaxed, that rides the same all day, so B inverts the physics. An HP candidate cannot run this step and stops at 0.50.
justification: Student floor about 0.50 by a student-available stem-relevance route (2x base); expert floor about 0.75. 0.50 is a real lift but short of the roughly 0.60 kill bar, so flag. The form channel this repair targeted is genuinely closed; what survives is a content pairing, and the surviving pair is the one the stem points at.

findings: Form is unusually tight and carries no isolate: all four options are exactly 15 words, all open with “She” plus a monotransitive verb, and none carries a hedge, a modal or an explicit negation.
WORLD_KNOWLEDGE / register, student-available but weak, eliminates D: a writer reporting instrumented readings will not rate “the trade’s brochures” the fuller answer. Residual of three at 0.33.
No cross-question support discriminates within A, B and C.
justification: Stems-only accuracy about 0.33 against a 0.25 base. One eliminable option is ordinary distractor quality, not a channel; the remaining three are separated only by a genre hunch about authorial modesty.

findings: Hedge balance is the prescribed 2+2 and is NOT scored: “probably” in A and “may” in D against flat B and C.

The lift comes from elsewhere: C over-reaches by naming exactly two determinants (“turns on the room’s temperature and the depth of the tines”) and A over-specifies a freezing mechanism, so both are eliminable on ordinary distractor-quality grounds, leaving B and D at 0.50.

The residual pair then happens to be one hedged against one flat, so the usual prefer-the-hedged heuristic picks D. This is not the prescribed-balance defect - the set is balanced - but the balance does not survive content elimination, which is worth recording even though it is not chargeable under the calibration.
CROSS_QUESTION (weak): q1 D and q2 C both make harrowing and tine depth salient, and q5 C names the tines again, tilting a reader toward the maintenance answer D.
Word counts descend monotonically 17/16/15/13: a gradient, not an isolate.
justification: Stems-only accuracy about 0.45 by a student-available two-step elimination. A real lift, below the roughly 0.60 kill bar, so flag.

Form balanced: modals 2/4 (“can” in B, “cannot” in C) against flat A and D; every option carries exactly one subordinate clause (“at the moment”, “before”, “because”, “once”); word counts 13/14/13/12. No form isolate.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, expert-only: haemolysis in pneumatic-tube transport is a deceleration artefact, which favours A, and haemolysis is not visible in whole blood before centrifugation, which marks B false. Neither step is available to an HP candidate.

findings: 3+1 exclusivity cluster (INERT, not scored): A, C and D all involve the railway survey, B attributes the quarrel to an untended thorn.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE, student-available: the stem asks what is implied. B states a cause outright (“The quarrel began because”) and C states bare chronology, so neither reads as an implication; the residual A and D sit at 0.50.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE / narrative schema, student-available: in a boundary quarrel that coincides with a railway survey, the hidden-motive reading - that the disputed ground is the pegged-out ground - is the one a strong reader reaches with no text in front of them. That is D.
Form balanced: word counts 14/13/13/14; no hedge or modal anywhere; the only negation-flavoured element is A’s “without bringing”, a 3+1 and inert.
justification: Stems-only accuracy about 0.47 by a route a strong student can run unaided: eliminate the two non-inferential options, then take the motive reading. A real lift, below the roughly 0.60 kill bar, so flag rather than kill.

findings: 3+1 exclusivity cluster (INERT, not scored): A, C and D are recommendations built on ”bör” that differ only in extent, while B characterises the ensemble’s objection instead.

Test-wise pulls cancel: the strongest-opinion heuristic points at B, while the answers-the-stem heuristic points away from B because it is about the ensemble rather than about textning. Net lift zero.

findings: No stems-only route: the four options are independent facts about a listing line, none entailed or excluded by another.

Weak single-variable isolates name different options and do not converge: C alone embeds a finite clause (”vem som sköter tekniken”), B alone carries a universal quantifier (”varje uppslag”). Word counts 6/7/6/6; no hedge, modal or negation anywhere.

findings: RULE 15 leg (a), one-way leak: NOT PRESENT, in either direction. q2’s option set supplies only a programme line, a loop symbol, audio description and school performances, none of which bears on the writer’s stance in q1. q1’s option set supplies stage sizes, a caption strip and ensemble resistance, none of which supplies the listing q2 presupposes. No proposition needed by one question survives three of four options in the other.

RULE 15 leg (b), symmetric vouching: NOT PRESENT. The two sets share only the accessibility-services topic, which is a frame, not a variable. No option in either question constrains the truth of an option in the other.
The propositions that do survive 4/4 in each set - that the theatre captions some performances, that a printed listing exists - are supplied by the stems themselves, so they are not leaks.

JOINT STEMS-ONLY FLOOR: 0.30 x 0.27 = 0.081, i.e. 1.3x the 6.25 percent base. The two questions are also uncorrelated - getting one right tells a student nothing about the other - so the independent product is the honest figure here.
justification: Both legs of RULE 15 are clean and the joint floor sits at base within estimation error. This is what a passing Swedish pair looks like, and it is the direct contrast to las-b22-003.

findings: Read alone the set is self-cancelling and would pass: it contains TWO contradictory pairs on TWO different variables - A vs B on whether the hooves coped, C vs D on whether the horses did this work - so the contradictory-pair heuristic privileges neither pair and yields no narrowing.

Read with its sibling it is not. q2’s option set supplies the proposition that people, not horses, moved the loads: ”delade på slitet” in A, ”på skidor av den som skulle ut” in C, ”Man fortsatte” in D. That contradicts q1 C (”Hästarna drog kälken i stället”) outright and undercuts q1 B, since hooves that coped would have been used.

Residual A and D at 0.50, and A takes the tilt because it is the option that explains why people rather than horses carried the loads: ”Hovarna sjönk igenom där folk gick” is the mechanism q2’s option set presupposes.
Unanchored deictic as a leak marker: ”i stället” in C has no antecedent in either stem, so the option is leaning on material outside its own question.
The route is student-available end to end: it needs only reading the sibling question’s options on the same page, and no domain knowledge at any step.
Form is clean and is not the problem here: word counts 6/5/5/7; subjects split 2+2 (”Hovarna” in A and B, ”Hästarna” in C and D); no hedge, modal, negation or consequence connective anywhere.
justification: Stems-only accuracy about 0.50 to 0.55 against a 0.25 base, by a student-available cross-question route. Within estimation error of the roughly 0.60 kill bar but not clearly over it, so flag at the question level; the kill is recorded on the pair line, where the structural defect actually lives.

findings: FORM PROFILE (the point of this pass). Consequence connective: 0/4 - neither så nor därför occurs anywhere in the set, so the variable is balanced and carries no isolate. Explicit negation: B alone (”inte”), 1/4, B isolated. Coordinate vs subordinate: A alone has no embedded clause at all (two finite VPs coordinated under “och”), while B embeds an infinitival, C a finite relative and D a finite temporal clause - A isolated. Absolutizers: A (distributive ”turades om”) and D (terminative ”sista lasset”), 2+2. Hedges and modals: B carries possibility modality (”Det gick inte att”) and C the past-future ”skulle” - 2+2 on surface modal auxiliaries, B alone on epistemic possibility. Opening word class: definite plural noun in A and C, non-referential pronoun in B (”Det”) and D (”Man”), 2+2. Word counts 7/8/10/7 - C overshoots the mode by three words. Longest verbatim-looking run: C’s ”på skidor av den som skulle ut” at seven words and the only concrete instrument in the set, against D’s ”tills sista lasset var hemma” at five, A’s ”delade på slitet” at three and B’s ”i förväg” at two. Voice: C is the only true agentive passive - the s-passive ”släpades” with an explicit av-phrase - whereas A’s ”turades” is a deponent s-form, not a passive, so on genuine agentive passive C stands alone.

IS ANY OPTION ISOLATED ON FORM? YES, AND IT IS C. A is isolated on clause structure and B on negation, but each on one variable only. C is isolated CONVERGENTLY on three variables at once - word count, agentive passive with an explicit av-phrase, and longest concrete run. Convergence across independent variables is what makes an isolate usable; a single-variable isolate is noise.

Content channel, a 2+2 contradictory pair on ONE variable, which is a channel by the binding calibration: A and C contradict each other on how the hauling was organised - collective rotation (”Hushållen turades om och delade på slitet”) against individual ad-hoc hauling (”av den som skulle ut”). B and D sit off that axis, so the heuristic narrows the set to A and C at 0.50 and the form isolate then picks C out of the pair.

FORM AND CONTENT CONVERGE ON THE SAME OPTION, and that option also carries the leak into q1. This is the opposite configuration to elf-b22-001 q3, where the weak form isolate and the content favourite are different options and cancel.
The only counter-pull is stem relevance: ”hur arbetet lades upp” reads as organisation, which flatters A and B, and it is what keeps this question below the kill bar on its own.
justification: Stems-only accuracy about 0.37 against a 0.25 base. A real lift from a convergent form isolate plus a contradictory pair, held under the roughly 0.60 kill bar only by the competing stem-relevance pull. Flag at the question level; the compound with q1 is charged on the pair line.

findings: RULE 15 leg (a), one-way leak: PRESENT, q2 into q1. The proposition is that people, not horses, moved the loads. It is positively supplied by THREE of q2’s four options - A (”Hushållen turades om och delade på slitet”), C (”Lassen släpades fram på skidor av den som skulle ut”) and D (”Man fortsatte tills sista lasset var hemma”) - and is contradicted by none of the four. Neither stem supplies it: q1 asks ”Vad sägs i texten om hästarna?” and q2 asks about ”hur arbetet lades upp”. It therefore survives whichever option is the key, which is exactly the robustness the three-of-four test is built to detect.
Effect of the leak: it contradicts q1 C, undercuts q1 B, leaves q1 at A/D 0.50 and tilts to A. It lifts q1 from about 0.27 read alone to about 0.50-0.55.

RULE 15 leg (b), symmetric vouching: PRESENT. q1 A (”Hovarna sjönk igenom där folk gick”) and q2 C (”Lassen släpades fram på skidor av den som skulle ut”) vouch for each other on one shared variable - who moved the loads and on what. Accept either and the other follows: hooves that break through where people do not entails a people-powered, weight-spreading mode, and skis entail that hooves were the thing that failed. The vouching closes a loop rather than running one way, so both legs fire on this pair.

JOINT STEMS-ONLY FLOOR, like-for-like with the previous measurement (independent product): 0.50 x 0.37 = 0.185, i.e. 2.96x the 6.25 percent base. The previous round measured roughly 2.9x. THE MULTIPLE IS UNCHANGED.

JOINT FLOOR, correlation-adjusted, which is the honest figure: the two questions are decided by ONE proposition, so outcomes are strongly positively correlated rather than independent - a student who reads the option sets as a people-hauled-on-skis scenario gets both, and one who does not gets neither. The correlated joint floor is near min(0.50, 0.37), about 0.35, i.e. about 5.6x base. The correlation is itself the defect, and it is worse than the product suggests.

CLOSED, MOVED, OR RENAMED: NOT CLOSED. This gate cannot compare option texts across rounds because the pre-repair candidates are out of scope for V-STEM, so the judgement rests on the measured multiple, which is flat at about 2.9x. What can be said is that the carrier is now nameable and sits ON the rewritten set: the explicit human-agent phrase ”av den som skulle ut” in q2 C, reinforced by ”delade på slitet” in q2 A. The leak has moved onto the repaired option set rather than off it.
Aggravating factor: the convergent form isolate in q2 names the SAME option that carries the leak, so form and content compound instead of cancelling. Whether or not that is new, it is live now.

KILL ROUTE, student-available end to end and needing no domain knowledge: read q2’s options first and conclude people hauled the loads; eliminate q1 C and q1 B; take q1 A. Then in q2 use the A-vs-C contradiction on collective versus individual organisation, and break the pair with C’s form isolation.
justification: Kill at the pair level. Both RULE 15 legs fire, the like-for-like multiple is unchanged at about 2.96x base against the roughly 2.9x the repair targeted, the correlation-adjusted floor is about 5.6x base, and the kill route is available to a passage-blind student with no expert knowledge. Neither question alone clears the roughly 0.60 bar - q1 about 0.50-0.55, q2 about 0.37 - but the pair is decided by a single leaked proposition and must be reworked as a unit: the human-agent material has to come out of q2’s options, or q1 has to stop asking about the horses’ role in the hauling.
